a:r.a:t: Polar Solutes Need Alternative Paths to Cross Cell Membranes

p:cNvPr.descr: An image illustrating energy changes accompanying passage of a hyrdrophilic solute through the lipid bilayer of a biological membrane. This image has a vertical image of the blue circles on both sides, with the inverted and upright V-shaped tubes in the middle. At the top left of this image is hydrated solute, illustrated as a red ball with reddish v-like images circling it. It has reversible arrows pointing to the vertical middle image’s edge. On the top and bottom of the arrows are the same reddish v-like images. The red ball is also in the middle of the vertical image in the middle. To the right of this image are reversible arrows pointing to the same image as on the left side, but the reddish v-like structures are closer to the ball. At the bottom of the vertical image in the middle is the same as the top, but it has a transporter in the middle. The reversible arrow point to the red ball in the middle, not to the edge. In the middle is a graph. The vertical axis is free energy, G. The horizontal axis is not marked. This has a red bell circle which dips in the middle, labeled as simple diffusion without transporter. This bell curve expands through the majority of the graph and at the top. From the top right of this curve is a dashed line going right horizontally. An arrow extends from the bottom of the red bell curve up to the dashed line, labeled as delta G simple diffusion [two-barred cross] simple diffusion. Below this is a smaller version of the red curve in blue and labeled as diffusion with transporter. It has a dashed line spanning across its top left curve and dashed horizontal line at the bottom. An arrow points from the dashed line at the bottom to the dashed line at the top, and is labeled as delta G [two-barred cross] transport.
